content: Hi how can i assist you today
News apps push articles on the exact topic I’m thinking—before I type anything.
Push topics usually derive from follow lists, location, and recent reads. Were you following tags or outlets tied to that topic?
I follow two tech feeds and had a tab open earlier.
That would influence the feed. Do these pushes appear after you read similar pieces, or also after unrelated browsing?
Mostly right after I read something adjacent.
Adjacent reading can seed recommendations. When you open a fresh session without sign-in, do the same topics surface as quickly?
They’re more generic in that case.
That contrast points to account signals. If a specific push feels uncanny, checking the ‘Why this story’ panel can reveal the trigger.
I didn’t know that panel existed; I’ll look for it.
It’s usually behind an info icon on the card. The reason listed often matches follows or location.
Okay, I’ll check it next time.
